headline.purpose: One per page: page title or ticket title.

body.purpose: Table cells, record text, field values, buttons.

meta.purpose: Table headers, location/asset lines, timeline actor lines, strip stop names, legend.

code.purpose: Ticket numbers, dates and times, counts, asset codes, file sizes, pagination numbers. Never Thai prose.

shadows.name: stop-active-ring
shadows.purpose: Current route stop being worked; timeline uses 2px/4px on the latest event.

shadows.name: stop-queued-halo
shadows.purpose: Current route stop waiting to be claimed.

shadows.name: row-hover-hairline
shadows.purpose: The one lifted thing: hovered queue row, with ink-100 fill.

shadows.name: field-focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Focused field, with border to ink-900.

motion.name: state-fast
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background changes on buttons, fields, nav tabs and rows. No other motion.

components.name: Route Strip
components.description: Signature five-stop route; state by form at fixed positions.

narrative.overview:
A repair ticket is a parcel moving between hands. Its status is its latest scan, the queue is a tracking board, and the detail page is the waybill with its scan history. Every screen sits under a postmark-indigo bar on pale label stock, with white hairline tables and panels carrying the work. The look is a logistics office, not a helpdesk: no sidebar, no floating cards, no coloured status pills.

Density comes first because IT staff work the queue all day on desktop. The queue uses three type sizes and ranks by weight and tabular figures, not by size. The one signature device is the five-stop route strip (แจ้งเรื่อง → ช่างระดับต้น → ช่างอาวุโส → อนุมัติอุปกรณ์ → ปิดงาน). Its stops sit at identical x positions on every row, so the queue lines up into columns of state. It repeats at full width on the detail page above the scan timeline.

Colour is rationed. Indigo ink does the structure, vermilion marks what can be pressed or what is critical, kraft means "waiting on someone else", and scan green means closed. Everything else is ink on white.
keyCharacteristics: Postmark-indigo top bar over a label-stock ground; white panels and tables ruled with 1px ink hairlines.
Five-stop route strip as the shared state vocabulary: filled, hollow, ringed or struck stops.
Anuphan for all UI text; JetBrains Mono only for ticket numbers, timestamps, counts and codes.
4px corners, 3px on small badges, full circles only for route stops and the scan timeline.
Flat: no drop shadows. The only shadows are ring outlines on stops, the hovered-row hairline and the field focus glow.

rules.name: The Pressable-or-Critical Rule
rules.body: Vermilion appears only on something you can press or focus (the primary action, the focus ring, the active nav tab), on critical or high priority, or on an error. A status label or decoration is never vermilion.

rules.name: The One Meaning Rule
rules.body: Kraft only means "waiting on someone outside IT", and scan green only means "closed". Neither colour is used for emphasis.

rules.name: The Three Sizes Rule
rules.body: A queue row uses only body and meta sizes plus mono. Rank inside a row comes from weight (400/500/600) and ink depth, never from a bigger size.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: Mono is reserved for identifiers, timestamps and figures. Thai prose, names and labels are never set in mono.

rules.name: The Fixed Stops Rule
rules.body: The compact strip is a fixed-width grid of five 12px stops with 20px gaps. It never stretches to its cell, so stops line up vertically down the whole queue.

rules.name: The One Lifted Thing Rule
rules.body: Only the hovered or focused row (or the focused control) is raised off the page, and it is raised with a hairline and a tint, not a shadow.

dos: Do use the route strip, at the same fixed stop positions, wherever a ticket's position matters, and pair it with the Thai status label.
Do set ticket numbers, dates, counts and codes in JetBrains Mono with tabular figures.
Do keep vermilion to the primary action, focus, active nav, critical/high priority and errors.
Do build new surfaces from panels (paper, 1px ink-200, 4px) on the label-stock ground under the indigo bar.
Do colour status as text only: ink-950 by default, kraft-700 for waiting, scan-700 for resolved, ink-500 for cancelled.
donts: Don't add a sidebar, floating white cards with drop shadows, or coloured status pills.
Don't use cast or elevation shadows; box-shadow is only for stop rings, the hovered-row hairline and focus.
Don't use kraft or scan green for emphasis or decoration; each carries exactly one state.
Don't set Thai labels, names or prose in mono, or enlarge type to rank items inside a dense row.
Don't carry the login page's IBM Plex, stone and signal-orange tokens into signed-in screens.
